correctness.rationale: Explicit state decomposition: root image top gives one map, fixed middle gives B_v, bottom gives A_v. Each nonleaf middle-root map reaches top; the bottom-root lifting condition is exactly coverage of all m middle labels. Inclusion-exclusion over missing labels yields the A_v product sum and the direct maximal-bottom-node proof gives the sharp branching threshold. The minimum-size argument forces m nonleaf children and m grandchildren. Full branching recurrence follows from identical child subtrees. \(A_{h+1}\ge A_h^d\) makes \(d^{-h}\log A_h\) monotone; counting all (m+2)^N functions bounds it. Independent direct finite function enumeration agreed for 1,928 parent-array/target cases, with 40 Stirling checks. The finite checks corroborate rather than prove the all-size conclusions.

originality.rationale: The precise theorem counts surjective single-relation reflexive-ancestor p-morphisms from arbitrary rooted trees to a fixed height-three fork \(Q_m\), with a sharp necessary-and-sufficient nonleaf-branch condition and regular-tree entropy. Closest inspected sources cover finite S4 tree semantics, modal preservation, and multi-relation ordered-tree morphisms, not this classification. The accessible previously published summaries on Boolean sources, weak-order sources, or ordinary continuous map counts have different domains or morphism conditions and do not imply this theorem. There remains risk from unindexed tree-automata and specialized p-morphism enumeration work.

value.rationale: A natural quotient-existence problem for finite S4 tree frames receives a complete source-structural characterization by m nonleaf children and a sharp \(2m+1\) world extremum. Exact labelled-map counts for every rooted-tree shape are obtained using two local states in \(O(m|T|)\) integer arithmetic operations, even when m is part of the input, and complete d-ary trees have a positive finite normalized log-count limit. These exact structural and computational consequences go beyond merely rephrasing the classical bounded-morphism definition.
